title: Le Verrier writes the law: an equation of its own, with no pieces and no hint
question: When the lab's hypotheses fail on a light curve, does Muse Wonder, given no building pieces and no hint of a mechanism, write a closed-form law that forecasts the unseen data better than those hypotheses, and does it write the point-lens law for gravitational microlensing events?
replay: uv run sira leverrier OID --leaps equation equation equation --out evidence/equations, on every object above: the lab bets every 10 days with its usual hypotheses (Ia, II, Ibc, TDE and none of them), and calls Le Verrier only at the first surprise, as in the team-size experiment
proposals: three equations per surprise, each from one call to Muse Wonder (muse-wonder-1.0, high effort) with the prompt below and the same blind case, failed hypotheses and misses
prompt: You are Le Verrier. The lab's hypotheses were fitted to this transient and their sealed forecasts failed on the measurements listed. Propose one new physical explanation and write it as a closed-form equation for the flux in each band as a function of time, which the lab's code will fit. Write expressions with numbers, t (days from now), your parameter and helper names, + - * / ^ ( ) and the functions sqrt, exp, log, abs, tanh, step, min, max; a parameter whose name ends in _b takes one value per band. Give every parameter a guess and a range. Say what your model predicts that the failed hypotheses do not. JSON: {"name": "a few words", "idea": "two sentences", "flux": "the flux of band b in microjansky", "helpers": {"name": "expression"}, "parameters": {"name": {"guess": number, "low": number, "high": number, "meaning": "words"}}, "predicts": "one sentence"}
reader: equations are parsed into a whitelist of numbers, t, the proposal's own parameter and helper names, + - * / ** and the functions abs, exp, log, max, min, sqrt, step, tanh; nothing the model writes is executed. Parameters need a guess and a range; 16 least-squares starts
choice: the lab keeps the equation with the lowest BIC on the data before the surprise; only its verdict counts
verdict: the sealed test of the team-size experiment: log e-value of the chosen equation (plus a 10% null) against the refitted old hypotheses on the next 40 days of data; Neptune at e >= 20, Vulcan at e <= 1/20, otherwise abstain

lens_law.rule: an equation writes the point-lens law when its flux or one of its helpers, without spaces and with ^ as ** and (t) removed, matches one of these patterns for the magnification (u^2+2)/(u*sqrt(u^2+4)); every equation is published so anyone can recount

report: on microlensing surprises: how many chosen equations write the lens law, how many of the three written per surprise do, and the chosen equations' verdicts
on surprises of every other class: the chosen equations' verdicts (a Neptune there is a false discovery) and any lens law written
the same lens surprises with the pieces of the team-size experiment, for comparison
cost, and every equation, fitted or not
before: a probe on three dev lenses (ZTF19aavisrq, ZTF19aavnrqt, ZTF22abgwuap) with an earlier prompt that still compared Le Verrier to the discovery of Neptune; that sentence was then removed as a hint of an unseen mass
a dev run of the final code on the same three dev lenses, nine equations: the lens law was chosen on two, and on the third, a lens, equations of a dusty red nova won their tests
after that dev run the lens-law patterns gained the form with u^2 as its own name, (u2+2)/(sqrt(u2)*sqrt(u2+4)); no test object had been replayed
disclosed: the role is still called Le Verrier
the blind case includes the galactic latitude rounded to 5 degrees, which astronomers also use
a flexible equation can win its test without being the right physics; the verdict and the lens law are reported apart
budget: about US$4: some ten surprises, three Wonder calls each
